findings: The project directory /Users/gokhanyetisken/Documents/GitHub/drydock/yrdy is empty: `ls -la` returns `total 0` and only `.` and `..`. No README, no config, no sources, no hidden files. There is nothing to survey and nothing to build on.

yrdy is not its own git repository: it has no .git, and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from inside it returns /Users/gokhanyetisken/Documents/GitHub/drydock. Its only tracked path is `yrdy/.drydock-out.json`, which git status currently reports as deleted (` D yrdy/.drydock-out.json`) because the harness unlinks it before each survey (engines.py:207-208).

The containing repository is drydock itself: a Python 3.13 harness (pyproject.toml, src/drydock/*.py, .venv holding fastapi 'starlette-1.10.0', uvicorn 0.54.0, anthropic, pydantic, pytest, ruff 0.17.5) that runs agent crews against other directories. The task sentence comes verbatim from its own skills/greenfield/SKILL.md:5 (`task: Build {what}. Tests from the first commit, and nothing is finished until they pass.`).

Toolchain detection is marker-file based and ordered: pom.xml, build.gradle, pyproject.toml, package.json (detect.py:22-67). yrdy matches none, so the toolchain is NOTHING with build_command "" and test_command "" (detect.py:73-80). Whichever marker the first item writes decides the commands for the rest of the run; detection is re-run after every item (orchestrate.py:42-45).

The commands are hard-wired per marker and cannot be configured by the project: package.json -> build `npm run build`, test `npm test` (detect.py:61-62); pyproject.toml -> build `uv sync --frozen`, test `uv run pytest -q` (detect.py:50-51).

The baseline for this run is builds=True with 0 tests run, 0 failed, 0 skipped, returned without executing anything because there is no build command (analyst.py:55-56). The run record for this exact task confirms it: runs/20261117-025031.json:3 has repo=.../yrdy, :4 the genco task string, :13 "tests_run": 0.

Three run records name yrdy (runs/20261117-015104.json, -015640.json, -025031.json). All three contain only a baseline with tests_run 0 and no plan, items, or results — no prior attempt on this directory got past the survey/baseline stage.

Six further run records carry the same genco/Italian-restaurant task against other directories. One of them did reach a plan: runs/20261117-022636.json (repo /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/bistro) holds an 11-item plan for an Astro 5 static site, plain CSS, no UI framework, Vitest 3, npm, Node 22, with item 1 being "package.json and an honest, failing test command" and deployment/README deliberately last.

Test counts are extracted from output by exactly two regexes: Maven Surefire's `Tests run: N, Failures: N, Errors: N, Skipped: N` and a pytest-shaped `(\d+) passed(?:,\s*(\d+) failed)?(?:,\s*(\d+) skipped)?` (parse.py:10-14). Any other format returns (0, 0, 0) (parse.py:35), and only the last 40 lines of output are parsed (shell.py:60-63 feeding verify.py:48).

Verification is: non-zero exit = fail (verify.py:50-51); then two arithmetic guards — "reported success but ran 0 tests" and "count dropped below baseline" — both gated on `base.tests_run` being non-zero (verify.py:54, 63). The baseline is captured once, before item 1 (session.py:97), and here it is 0.

Git handling, all with cwd = yrdy: the run starts with `git checkout -B drydock/<run-id>` (orchestrate.py:53-54), each passing item is `git add -A` + `git commit` (repo.py:32-38), each failing item is undone with `git reset --hard -q HEAD` + `git clean -fdq` (repo.py:40-43), and the engineer stage refuses to start unless `git status --porcelain` is empty (orchestrate.py:47-51, repo.py:22-23).

The engineer's shell is a single allowlist entry derived from the build command: `Bash(<first word> *)` once a build file exists, otherwise the 17-name BOOTSTRAP list — npm, npx, pnpm, yarn, node, python, python3, uv, pip, pip3, go, cargo, mvn, gradle, dotnet, mkdir, ls, cat (engines.py:48-81, used at engines.py:140). `git` is not on either list.

Engine choice changes what is possible: the ClaudeCodeEngine engineer gets `Read Edit Write Glob Grep` plus that one Bash rule (engines.py:139-140), while the API-engine engineer gets only write_file, replace_in_file and a `build` tool that runs build_command (tools.py:106-184) — it has no way to install a dependency at all.

Local toolchain: node v22.21.0 with npm, npx and yarn under ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.21.0/bin; uv, mvn, yarn and python3 under /opt/homebrew/bin. No pnpm, no bun. Commands are run with shlex.split and no shell, inheriting the harness process PATH (shell.py:30-45).

drydock/.gitignore is 13 lines: __pycache__/, .env, .venv, .venv/, *.egg-info, *.py[oc], build/, dist/, runs/, wheels/. It does not ignore node_modules, .next, .astro, dist inside yrdy (only top-level `dist/`), .drydock-report.json or .drydock-out.json, and there is no yrdy/.gitignore.

The diff inspector is deterministic and fires on: removed test declarations outnumbering added ones (`@Test`, `def test`, `func Test`, `\b(?:it|test)\s*[(.]`, `#[test]`, `[Test]`), added lines matching SILENCER (`.skip(`, `.todo(`, `xit(`, `xdescribe(`, `@Disabled`...), a net loss of 3+ lines matching `\bassert|\bexpect\s*\(|\bshould\b` case-insensitively, and added files named like secrets (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.p12`, `credentials.json`) (inspect.py:21-63, 102-137).

What the task does not say, and has to be decided: the stack and whether there is a build step at all; whether any page is dynamic (reservations, contact form) or the site is wholly static; the address and neighbourhood (none given); opening hours; the menu — dishes, categories, prices; phone and email; how reservations are taken (phone, form, OpenTable); whether ordering/delivery is in scope; one page or several; photography and brand assets (none are committed, and nothing in the repo can supply them); logo, typography, palette; metadata/SEO; accessibility target; analytics; hosting and domain; and what counts as finished. The name is given only as lower-case "genco".

The skill's own bar is explicit and is the acceptance criterion here: the tests must exist, run, and pass, all three, because "a suite that passes because it contains nothing is the failure this skill is written to prevent" (skills/greenfield/SKILL.md:56-63), and the first item must be the skeleton whose test command exists and fails on an empty suite (SKILL.md:27-31, architect.py:35-37).
risks: The engineer stage will likely abort before item 1. `is_clean()` runs `git status --porcelain` with cwd=yrdy, which reports the whole drydock repository, and `yrdy/.drydock-out.json` is tracked at HEAD and is deleted then rewritten by every survey. So the tree is dirty the moment this survey runs, and orchestrate.py:47-51 raises SystemExit("... has uncommitted changes"). The three yrdy run records that stop at a baseline with no plan are consistent with the run never reaching that point. This must be resolved first — commit the file, or ignore it — and it is a property of the harness checkout, not of anything the website code can fix.

Rollback is repository-wide. `git reset --hard -q HEAD` (repo.py:42) with cwd inside yrdy resets all of drydock, so one failed item discards any uncommitted edit anywhere in the harness checkout — including edits to src/drydock made while a run is in flight. `git clean -fdq` then deletes untracked files from yrdy downwards.

`git checkout -B drydock/<run-id>` (orchestrate.py:53-54) moves the drydock repository itself off `main`, and because each item commits with `git add -A` at the repo root, any unrelated dirty file in drydock gets folded into that item's commit under a message like "1. package.json and an honest, failing test command". Harness changes would be mis-attributed to restaurant-website items.

node_modules will be committed into the drydock repository unless the very first item creates yrdy/.gitignore in the same item as package.json. Nothing in drydock/.gitignore covers node_modules, yrdy has no .gitignore, and the per-item commit is `git add -A` at the repo root. An Astro or Next install is tens of thousands of files.

The count ratchet the skill asks for never engages on this project. Both arithmetic guards in verify.py are conditioned on `base.tests_run` (verify.py:54, 63), the baseline is taken once before item 1 (session.py:97), and here it is 0 — for the whole run. So a later item that stops discovering tests, or a runner misconfigured to find none, passes verification on exit code alone; the only remaining check is inspect.py counting removed test declarations in the diff. "Watch the count from the first item onwards" (SKILL.md:62) has to be done by reading the reported numbers, because the harness will not fail the item.

Consequently the empty-suite trap is live and unguarded: if `npm test` can exit 0 having found nothing — `vitest --passWithNoTests`, `jest --passWithNoTests`, a `|| true` in the script, or a glob that matches no file — every later green run means nothing and the verifier cannot tell. Vitest's default (non-zero when no test files are found) is the only thing making item 1's "must fail on an empty suite" requirement work; a vitest.config.js or a flag added later silently removes it.

Choosing node's built-in runner would make every item report zero tests. `node --test` summarises as `# pass N` / `# fail N`, which matches neither regex in parse.py:10-14, so read_test_counts returns (0, 0, 0) and the verdict text becomes "0 tests pass" even on a green suite. Vitest ("Tests  2 passed (2)") and jest ("Tests: 2 passed") do match the pytest-shaped pattern; pick a runner whose summary contains "N passed".

Failure counts are mis-read when failures print before passes. The regex requires ", N failed" to follow "N passed" (parse.py:14), but jest prints "Tests: 1 failed, 2 passed, 3 total" and vitest "Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)". Group 1 captures the passed count and the failed group stays empty, so the verdict reads "0 tests failing" on a red run. The item still fails on exit code, but the reason handed back to the engineer as `failure` text (orchestrate.py:87) is wrong, which costs a retry loop.

If package.json is the marker, the build command is fixed at `npm run build`. A plain static HTML/CSS site has nothing to build, and any item with verify_with="build" runs only that command and nothing else (verify.py:39-45), so it fails unless package.json defines a `build` script that exits 0. Equally, `npm test` with no "test" script exits non-zero, so every tests item fails until the script exists. Both scripts have to land in the first item.

Items verified with "build" do not run the suite at all (verify.py:39-45). In the earlier plan for this same task, 5 of 11 items were build-verified (runs/20261117-022636.json:99,110,121,146,156) — in a plan shaped like that, more than a third of the items are accepted without any test ever running, and with the ratchet inactive nothing catches up later.

Once a build file exists, the engineer's Bash allowlist narrows to one tool: `Bash(npm *)` for package.json (engines.py:78-80). `npx`, `node`, `mkdir`, `ls` and `cat` are available only while the repository still has no build file — i.e. during item 1. Any scaffolding that needs `npx create-...` or a one-off `node` script must happen in that item or not at all, and the API engine cannot run even that (tools.py:138-141 gives it build_command only).

Commands are launched with shlex.split and no shell, inheriting the harness process's PATH (shell.py:30-45), and node/npm here are nvm-managed under ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.21.0/bin. If drydock is started from anything other than a shell with nvm on PATH, `npm test` returns exit 127 from FileNotFoundError (shell.py:43-44) and is reported as a failing suite rather than a missing runner — a confusing failure that will be blamed on the tests.

A Python stack is the worse bet of the two. `uv sync --frozen` (detect.py:50) fails unless a uv.lock is committed, so the first item would have to produce one with a command it may not be able to run; and a new yrdy/pyproject.toml sits inside a directory tree whose parent is already a uv project (drydock/pyproject.toml with its own .venv), so uv's parent-directory discovery needs checking before committing to it. The marker order (detect.py:22-67) also means that if both pyproject.toml and package.json ever exist in yrdy, pyproject wins and the npm commands become unreachable.

Content edits can trip the honesty inspector. ASSERTION matches the bare word "should" case-insensitively (inspect.py:46) and the "assertions removed" finding fires at a net loss of three such lines (inspect.py:124-133); TEST_DECLARATION matches `\b(?:it|test)\s*[(.]` (inspect.py:26). On a restaurant site most of the diff is prose — menu descriptions, an About paragraph — so a copy rewrite that drops a few sentences containing "should", or text where "it (" appears, is reported as weakening the suite and sends the item back. The earlier plan already flagged the related hazard of menu copy edits breaking the menu test (runs/20261117-022636.json:31).

Adding any file named `.env`, `.env.local`, `*.pem`, `*.p12` or `credentials.json` is rejected outright (inspect.py:60-63, 135-137). A working reservation form, a mail service key or an analytics ID cannot be configured in the repository, so either the site stays static with no secrets, or configuration is explicitly declared out of scope.

The task supplies none of the facts a restaurant site is made of — no address, hours, menu, prices, or phone number. Whatever the engineer writes will be invented, and a test that asserts an invented price or an invented closing time locks the invention in and makes it look verified. Keep invented content in one clearly-marked placeholder module, assert its shape rather than its values, and say in the report that the content is placeholder — otherwise a green suite will read as a finished, factual site.

There is no .git in yrdy today, so if this folder is (re-)added through the harness UI, workspace.add_project runs `git init` + `git add -A` + an initial commit inside it (workspace.py:103-109). That would create a repository nested in drydock's working tree and silently change what every later git call in the run means — repo-wide commits and resets would become yrdy-scoped mid-stream. Safer, but a different set of rules than the ones this survey describes; check which state the project is in before trusting either.

"Genco" as the name of an Italian restaurant in New York is a Godfather reference (Genco Olive Oil, Genco Abbandando). Copy, imagery or taglines leaning on the film are third-party IP and a branding decision nobody has made; the task gives only the lower-case name and no styling. Default to treating it as a plain family name and flag the choice rather than making it in the copy.
